say.text: Final check. These are fresh stems on earlier ideas, and the last three give no hints.
A student sketches Hesselbach's triangle and draws the deep inguinal ring as its lateral side. Which correction is right?

choices.label: Nothing is wrong: the deep ring is the lateral corner
The artery is the lateral side; the deep ring lies outside it
The lateral side is the superficial ring, an aponeurotic opening
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: A three-sided patch has sides, and the wall has openings. Which of these two things is the lateral boundary?
Not correct. The deep ring is an opening in the fascia, not a side; the lateral side is the inferior epigastric artery.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the ring lies outside the triangle, lateral to the artery.

say.text: Yes. The sides are the inferior epigastric artery laterally, the rectus sheath edge medially and the inguinal ligament below.
The deep ring is an opening outside that patch. Exam keys use the inguinal ligament as the base, not Cooper's ligament.
Not quite. The superficial ring is an opening of the anterior wall's external oblique aponeurosis, so it cannot be a side of the triangle.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the artery, the rectus edge and the inguinal ligament are the three sides.

say.text: In the invagination test the little finger pushes scrotal skin into the superficial ring. On coughing, the impulse strikes the very tip of the fingertip.
Which hernia is suggested?

choices.label: Direct inguinal hernia, the pulp sign
Indirect inguinal hernia, the tip sign
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Two fingertip sites, two sacs: one runs down the cord, one is pushed straight forward. Which depth goes with which?
That is not right. A pulp impulse suggests direct; this tip impulse points the other way.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: tip means indirect and pulp means direct.

say.text: Not correct. The ring finger belongs to Zieman's three-finger test, a different test from this one.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: Zieman's finger sites and this test's tip and pulp are separate.

say.text: Yes. In the invagination test an impulse on the tip suggests indirect and on the pulp suggests direct.
The ring finger is Zieman's femoral site and has no place in this test.
Same bedside manoeuvre on two men, deep ring held shut after reduction. A: on coughing, nothing comes back. B: on coughing, a lump bulges medial to your finger.
Who has the direct hernia?

choices.label: A, because the finger held a direct sac back
Neither, because the test cannot separate the two
B, because the sac slipped past the finger medially
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: The finger blocks only one entrance. Which sac uses that entrance, and which one avoids it?
Not quite. The finger shuts the deep ring, the entrance for the indirect sac, so a held-back sac is indirect.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the ring test controls the indirect sac only.

say.text: That is not right. It can: an indirect hernia is controlled by the finger, whereas a direct one still appears medial to it.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the result differs by type, and that is the point of the test.

say.text: Yes. A direct sac comes through the posterior wall medial to the finger, so it still appears when the ring is held shut.
A, controlled by the finger, is the indirect hernia that uses the deep ring.
Two men with reducible groin hernias. One has a huge, long-standing direct bulge; the other a small indirect hernia that runs down the cord.
Which is more likely to strangulate, and why?

choices.label: The huge direct one, as more bowel means more twist
The small indirect one, as its deep-ring neck is narrow
The huge direct one, as a wide sac drags its neck tight
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Strangulation is a squeeze at the neck. Compare the two necks, not the two lumps.
Not correct. Size does not set the risk, and direct hernias are the classic type that rarely strangulates.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: judge the neck, not the bulk.

say.text: Yes. A narrow neck at the deep ring makes an indirect hernia more liable to strangulate than a direct one.
Bulk does not set the risk; the neck does.
Not quite. A direct hernia has the wider neck and the lower risk; indirect carries more risk than direct.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the narrow neck belongs to the indirect hernia.

say.text: A student writes: 'Of all groin hernias, the indirect one most often strangulates, because indirect is the commonest.'
Which correction is right?

choices.label: Direct strangulates more often than indirect, so direct
Indirect is commonest; femoral strangulates most in the groin
The student is right, since groin and inguinal mean the same
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: What does 'groin' include that 'inguinal' leaves out, and which of those has the tightest neck?
That is not right. Direct is the classic answer for the hernia that rarely strangulates.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: indirect carries more risk than direct, and femoral more than both.

say.text: Yes. 'Commonest' and 'most likely to strangulate' are different questions; indirect leads the first.
'Groin' is wider than 'inguinal' and takes in femoral, which has the highest strangulation risk of the groin hernias.
Not correct. 'Groin' also takes in femoral hernias, and femoral has the highest strangulation risk among them.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: read the scope word before you answer.

say.text: A theatre list reads: 'Boy, 8 months, right inguinal hernia: Lichtenstein repair.'
Which correction is right?

choices.label: Change to Bassini, since a tissue repair avoids foreign mesh
Change to herniotomy, since only the sac needs removing
No change: mesh repair suits every age
Not sure, give me a hint

say.text: Ask what has failed in a child: the sac channel or the posterior wall?
Not quite. A child's posterior wall is normal, so no wall repair of any kind is needed.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: the child's defect is the sac, not the wall.

say.text: Yes. The child's defect is a patent processus vaginalis with a normal posterior wall, so herniotomy alone is the operation.
Adult repairs that rebuild the wall are not needed.
That is not right. Mesh reinforces a weak adult wall; a child's wall is normal and the sac alone is removed.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: match the operation to the defect, not to the habit.

say.text: No hints from here. Which patient is best served by open Lichtenstein rather than laparoscopic repair?

choices.label: A man with bilateral hernias, surgeon trained in laparoscopy
A man with a primary unilateral hernia, surgeon trained only in open repair
A man with recurrence after open repair, surgeon trained in laparoscopy

say.text: Not correct. Bilateral hernias are among the cases laparoscopic repair is preferred for.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: bilateral and recurrent hernias favour laparoscopy.

say.text: Not quite. Recurrence after open repair is the other case where laparoscopic repair is preferred.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: recurrence after open repair points to laparoscopy.

say.text: Yes. Bilateral hernias and recurrence after open repair are the usual laparoscopic cases.
A primary unilateral hernia suits laparoscopy only in experienced hands; here open Lichtenstein is the standard.
A hospital offers open repair only. Its patient is a 55-year-old with a primary unilateral hernia. Which operation is the current standard?

choices.label: Bassini repair, the classic open operation
Shouldice repair, the best tissue repair

say.text: Not correct. Bassini is a tissue repair under tension, and it is not the current standard.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: older keys expected Bassini; current practice is Lichtenstein.

say.text: That is not right. Shouldice is the best tissue repair, but it is not the standard open repair.
Keep both keys: older PYQs expected Bassini, and current practice is Lichtenstein mesh.
Yes. Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is the standard open adult repair.
Older PYQs expected Bassini, and Shouldice is the best tissue repair.
At operation, a hernia sac is found to contain a Meckel's diverticulum.
Which eponym fits?
Not quite. Amyand's holds the appendix in an inguinal sac, not a Meckel's diverticulum.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: Amyand's is an appendix eponym.

say.text: That is not right. De Garengeot holds the appendix in a femoral sac, not a Meckel's diverticulum.

sure_note.text: You were sure, so recheck: de Garengeot is also an appendix eponym.

say.text: Yes. Littre's hernia is the one with Meckel's diverticulum in the sac.
Amyand's is the appendix in an inguinal sac, and de Garengeot's the appendix in a femoral sac.
That closes the module. Carry three rules: the triangle's sides come from the artery, the rectus edge and the ligament; the nerve follows the approach; the eponym follows the site.
The cards next keep the rules on a spacing schedule.

cards.q: What bounds Hesselbach's triangle, and which inferior boundary do exam keys expect?
cards.a: Inferior epigastric artery laterally, rectus sheath medially, inguinal ligament below. Exam keys use the inguinal ligament, not Cooper's ligament.

cards.q: Most common groin hernia, and most common hernia in children?
cards.a: Indirect inguinal hernia in both cases; inguinal is the commonest abdominal wall hernia.

cards.q: Which groin hernia strangulates most, and why does the neck matter?
cards.a: Femoral hernia among groin hernias. An indirect hernia's narrow neck at the deep ring makes it strangulate more than a direct one.

cards.q: Which operation for a bilateral or recurrent hernia, and which for a primary unilateral adult hernia?
cards.a: Laparoscopic TEP or TAPP for bilateral or recurrent; open Lichtenstein tension-free mesh for a primary unilateral adult hernia.

cards.q: Amyand's versus de Garengeot's versus Littre's?
cards.a: Amyand's: appendix in an inguinal sac. De Garengeot's: appendix in a femoral sac. Littre's: Meckel's diverticulum.
